## Purpose
Hides controls the signed-in person's role does not allow, by evaluating the server's own route policy (`GET /api/auth/policy`) against the exact endpoint each control calls. A button is shown exactly when the server would accept its request.

## Responsibilities
- **`usePolicy()`:** query key `["auth","policy"]`, stale and gc time Infinity, retry 2.
- **`useAllowed()`** returns `(method, path) => boolean`:
  - false until the policy has loaded;
  - strips the API prefix;
  - finds the first rule whose methods and regex match; no match is false;
  - the access kinds: public and self are always allowed; user needs a user; any needs a user or an admin; admin needs an admin; perm allows an admin when `admin_ok`, else any of the user's permissions.
- **The rest of the file** (154 lines) holds helper components that hide or mark read-only controls (the Eye icon is used for "view only").

## Key elements
`usePolicy`, `useAllowed`.

## Control flow
React Query plus a memoised regex compile.

## Data, state and side effects
None.

## Configuration
None.

## Interactions
- **Backend:** `/api/auth/policy` (`app/auth/permissions.py`).
- **Used by:** action buttons across the pages.

## Error handling and edge cases
- Write controls never flash in before the policy is known.

## Nuances and gotchas
- **It uses the same first-match rules as the server.** Presentation only; the server enforces.

As described.
